methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents deliberate capability-building outside metro centers, creating potential peer learning networks that could distribute AI fluency through educational institutions in mid-sized markets—a key mechanism for the 'Build It Yourself' pathway.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA explicitly targets community-wide AI education and innovation, not just enterprise adoption—signaling intentional infrastructure for distributed, deep learning that could spread beyond traditional tech sectors into Richmond's broader workforce.

signals.title: How Fairfax County police are using AI — and why opponents are concerned - NBC4 Washington
signals.signal_reading: Fairfax County police deploying AI with organized opposition reflects the concentration of both advanced implementation capacity and sophisticated governance discourse in NoVA—capabilities and debates largely absent from rural Virginia jurisdictions.

signals.title: How AI is changing what happens to Hampton Roads' trash - The Suffolk News-Herald
signals.signal_reading: AI adoption in waste management represents platform-delivered automation reaching municipal operations—shallow but practical application that could distribute across regions without requiring deep local technical expertise, though limited to operational efficiency gains.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Richmond's young workforce feeling AI pressure without corresponding reports of systematic skill-building infrastructure suggests anxiety outpacing capability development—a warning signal that awareness alone doesn't translate to competitive readiness.
